P1.evidence: No setter, but the application was genuinely read and fed back twice during the call — 'I saw in your application that you were ripped and quite fit before' and the prospect's own 'one of the things that I put in the application was that I just want to have the mobility to play with my kid' — which is the check doing its job. Frame is the usual three-part version. Agreement asked and given, open question asked verbatim.

P2.evidence: Weight was asked directly ('what are we talking about? Is it like 200, 185?') producing 83.5 kg, with height established and age surfacing in the why question. The injury probe was excellent: the 1-to-10 scale run separately for back and shoulder, duration asked ('How long have you had it for?'), and the functional detail extracted — lateral movements hurt, overhead is restricted, daily life is fine. Training was well covered and the rep caught his own gap mid-presentation: 'I actually didn't ask, but how many steps do you think you're setting a day?' Diet was thoroughly probed and produced keto day eight, the eating window, the smoking-cravings link and his diet history. Against that: health conditions were never asked, sleep was never mentioned, energy was never asked despite being a stated goal, and the eight-to-ten-hour seated workday was volunteered rather than elicited.

P3.evidence: The best-executed goals phase in the batch. The bridge ran twice and produced the age-40 realisation and the scale moment. The future-pace was well framed against his specific doubt — 'imagine in six months your mobility is half as severe as it is at the moment, how would that be for you?' — and produced the deepest answer on the call: 'I'd be proud of myself because I set a goal and I'm keeping my word to myself. I didn't let myself down.' And P3h ran properly, which almost never happens elsewhere in this batch: 'when you would have just had to go off getting ripped, getting a better body, that would have been a nice goal, but then work gets busy and the first thing you'd throw out the window is the training. But when you give that reason that you want to be able to play with your son those four years... that sounds like that's the actual reason.' Only P3f is soft — the son came from the application and was reinforced rather than asked about.

P4.evidence: Past attempts, outcomes and root causes all surfaced with real specificity: the Frank Medrano calisthenics programme that got him shredded and then injured, and the carnivore diet that worked and was abandoned. The prospect named both gaps himself, precisely — on the programme, 'it's not personalized... how could I know if my form was right or wrong if I'm just following a video? And I got hurt'; on the diet, 'I feel great, but I'm not enjoying the process of feeling great'. The need question ran ('what do you feel like you would need in order to actually get to the outcome?') and, pressed again later, produced the sentence the whole sale rests on: 'I just want to feel that there's someone supporting me through this journey.' P4f was never asked as a question, but the reframe ran in an adapted form and landed — 'probably when you began with poker, you had to learn from someone, right? And now you just know what you're doing.'

P5.evidence: The settle question ran almost verbatim — 'do you feel like you're willing to settle for the fact where it only gets worse or sort of stays the same for the next 10, 20 years?' — and got a firm 'No, no. I couldn't settle for that.' But the cost of inaction was built by the prospect, not the rep: 'I'm 40, how can I have back pain? If I'm 50, what's gonna happen?' and 'either I keep living this way and when I'm 50 I'm just gonna be laying down in a bed.' The rep's contribution was one line of amplification, 'it won't get better, I can tell you that'. Why-not was never asked and the line in the sand was asserted rather than requested. The phase worked because this prospect did the work himself.

P6.evidence: Belief was tested and confirmed — 'when we have all that in place, you are going to be able to get to those goals?' answered 'Yeah. Perfect.' The rep then asked an excellent supplementary question that is not in the script and should be: 'is there something specific that stands out to you the most, that's really what we need to double down on?' The answer, 'I just want to feel that there's someone supporting me through this journey', is the single most useful line in the transcript. The go-all-in question was never asked in its 'is there any reason you wouldn't' form, only in the positive. Sequencing was clean — price came only after the yes, and the prospect had already volunteered 'I'm locked in' and 'I'm 100% committed' well before it.

P11.evidence: The weakest close execution in the batch, on the easiest deal in the batch. Step 1: a payment link was sent to the Zoom chat and to WhatsApp and receipt was confirmed, but nothing was collected — the card was at an office fifteen minutes away, the rep floated fetching it ('if it's in the same house, just take a quick walk and get it') and then accepted a two-hour deferral. Step 2: a Trevor slot was proposed for 13:15 the next day and a link sent, but both parties treated the booking as contingent on payment, so it is provisional. Steps 3 and 4 did not happen at all — no agreement email, no signature, no welcome email, no Skool community link, no onboarding questionnaire, none of it mentioned. Contrast the Scott Hamilton call in this same batch, where all four steps ran in order.

objection_plays.detail: A genuine fear-and-doubt trigger, though about capability rather than the offer: 'it's hard for me to believe that I can do this, or grab a kettlebell with the pain that I feel when I do these exercises.' The rep answered it twice and effectively, in substance if not to script — Trevor's own history of shoulder and back injuries, then progressive loading ('we're not going to start with super heavy weights, first of all because of your shoulder'), reinforced with a poker analogy about starting at five-dollar stakes. That is the scripted BRIDGE move — not asking him to see the whole other side, just take the first step — arriving in the prospect's own language. None of the other OE moves ran (certainty, pleasure versus pain, the plane, burned before), and none were needed. The prospect resolved it himself: 'that's why I applied because he said he used to suffer from it.'
No hesitation whatsoever. He had pre-committed before hearing the price.
A girlfriend is mentioned in passing but never as a decision-maker. He decided alone.
Zero money objection. He asked one question about structure — one-time or monthly — accepted the answer and said 'Sounds good.' Correctly treated as logistics rather than resistance.
The opposite: he had already started the diet and stated he would proceed regardless of whether he worked with Trevor.

Gap: a ready buyer without his card to hand. Not an objection and not affordability — the money exists and the decision is made, but the instrument is fifteen minutes away. There is no scripted move for holding a sold buyer through to collection, and the rep improvised weakly: he suggested fetching it, was told two hours, and settled for a second Zoom instead. Two hours is enough time for a poker professional to get distracted, and the whole Phase 11 sequence now depends on a call that may not happen. A scripted line for 'go and get the card, I'll wait' would have closed this on the day.

notes: Phases 3, 4 and 6 were the strongest of the batch — the reflect-back genuinely ran, the root cause came out in the prospect's own words twice, and the extra question 'what should we double down on?' produced the sentence that sold the deal. Then the close was left half-finished. This buyer had said 'I'm locked in' before the price, accepted $6,000 in one breath, and still walked away without paying, without an agreement, without the community link and without a confirmed onboarding call, because his card was in another building and the rep took two hours as an answer. That is the coaching point: on a zero-resistance close, ask him to go get the card and hold the line. Separately, escalate that a prospect with several years of chronic back pain and a restricted overhead shoulder — who is flying to Dallas in September to see a chiropractor about it, and who named that exact doubt himself — was reassured with the coach's personal injury history rather than any assessment.
